newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Dec CPI up 2.52 pct, full '96 rise 3.07 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Dec CPI up 2.52 pct, full '96 rise 3.07 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's consumer price index was up 2.52 percent in December compared to December 1995, bringing the full-year 1996 CPI rise to 3.07 percent, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Monday.

At the wholesale level, December's wholesale price index was down 3.57 percent compared to December 1995, resulting in a full-year 1996 wholesale price index fall of 0.99 percent, the statistics agency said in its monthly report.
In month-to-month terms, December's consumer price index was down 0.69 percent compared to November, while December's wholesale price index was down 0.28 percent from November, the agency said.

The agency said the 1996 consumer price rise was the lowest in three years, following rises of 3.7 percent in 1995 and 4.1 in 1994, and mainly reflected falling international raw material prices and slowing rates of local rent and wage increases.

The annual 3.07 percent CPI rise was well below an official government projection of 3.5 percent issued at the beginning of 1996 and slightly below the most recent projection of 3.1 percent issued in November.

Agency officials said an average nine percent rise in domestic oil prices authorised by the government on January 1 would result in a 0.39 percentage point increase in January's consumer price index but that the effect would be offset somewhat by soft global prices for material prices.
"The lower international raw material prices will contribute to an increase in 1997 consumer prices that is less than we had projected," said Tsai Mei-na, an agency section chief.
December's relatively low CPI increase reflected falling prices for vegetables and milk as well as year-end discounting in department stores, the agency said.
